review_notes: I read the whole file. I searched Mathlib for any existing monoidal structure or tensor product on `Mat_ C` (patterns "MonoidalCategory (Mat_" and "Mat_.*Monoidal") and found none. I listed the declarations in Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Preadditive/Mat.lean. It has the category, preadditive and biproduct structure, `mapMat_`, `embedding`, `lift` and the equivalence lemmas. It has no tensor, Kronecker, associator or unitor construction, and no reindexing-by-equivalence morphism that the diagonal `matAssocHom` or unitor definitions could reuse. The new definitions (`matTensorObj`, `matTensorHom`, `matTensorUnit`, `matAssociator`, the unitors and `matMonoidal`) are therefore the first such structure and do not compete with an existing one. The `mat_comp_*_apply` lemmas are specialisations of `Mat_.comp_apply`. The rubric excludes theorem duplication, and these lemmas are not a competing concept. I did not check the sibling files MatBraided and MatEmbMonoidal in the same repo, because only duplication against Mathlib, Batteries and core is in scope. I have no remaining doubt about the Mathlib side.
